name: Pipedrive
fit: Your team mainly needs deals, email sync and reliable follow-up.
billing: Growth, annual billing; see price note below
catch: Web calling needs another provider. LeadBooster, documents and campaigns can add to the bill.
good: Growth includes full email sync, tracking, automations and follow-up sequences. The visual pipeline gives reps a straightforward way to manage deals and the next activity.
limit: Browser calling needs a connected phone provider. Marketing campaigns and advanced document tools are separate add-ons.
cost: Growth is listed at $24 per user per month, billed annually; see the price difference noted above. LeadBooster, Smart Docs, Projects and Campaigns cost extra.
verdict: Choose Growth for a straightforward sales pipeline and email follow-up. Budget separately for the phone system and marketing tools you need.
check: Import a live deal, send an email and assign its next call. Check that the rep can see all three without rebuilding the record.

name: Close
fit: Reps spend much of the day calling and following up.
catch: The cheaper Essentials plan has no automated workflows. Phone numbers and usage cost extra.
good: Growth combines the pipeline, email, automated workflows and a power dialer. Calls and follow-up can stay on the same lead record, which suits a busy calling team.
limit: Existing HubSpot activities need a separate migration from your contacts. Plan how to move the history and rebuild your automations.
cost: Growth costs $99 per user per month on annual billing, or $109 month to month. Essentials costs $35 or $49 on those terms but leaves out workflows. Add numbers, calling, SMS and optional AI usage.
verdict: Choose Close Growth if your reps spend the day calling and following up. The power dialer and workflows are built in. Phone usage costs extra.
check: Test an unanswered call, a scheduled callback and a handoff to another rep. Confirm that the history and next task survive the migration.

name: Zoho CRM
fit: You want email, workflows and follow-up at a low seat price.
catch: Someone must own the configuration. Calling numbers and usage consume paid credits.
good: Standard already includes email integration, workflow rules and Cadences for follow-up. You do not need Professional simply to get a sequence of sales activities.
limit: Cadence and automation limits depend on the edition. Someone must own field setup and follow-up rules.
cost: Standard is $14 per user monthly on annual billing or $20 month to month. Built-in telephony charges for numbers and usage. Supporting Team User licences have restricted access and do not replace full sales licences.
verdict: Start with Standard when subscription cost is the priority. It already covers email, workflows and Cadences. Upgrade when you hit a limit that affects the work.
check: Have the person who will maintain Zoho build one follow-up sequence. Check how replies stop it and who receives the next task.

name: Freshsales
fit: You want a sales CRM with built-in calling and sequences.
catch: Growth's $9 annual rate excludes sales sequences. Phone usage needs paid credits.
good: Freshsales combines contact and deal management with email and phone tools. Pro adds sales sequences and more automation, making it the relevant tier for repeated follow-up.
limit: Pro allows ten sales sequences per user. Phone credits sit outside the licence price.
cost: Pro costs $39 per user per month on annual billing, or $47 month to month. Growth costs $9 or $11 on those terms. Phone numbers, inbound and outbound calls, and some calling features consume prepaid credits.
verdict: Choose Pro for built-in calling and sales sequences at a lower licence cost than HubSpot Professional. The cheaper Growth plan leaves out sequences.
check: Run a short calling session, inspect credit use and check the follow-up record. Include an old HubSpot note and completed activity in the migration sample.

name: monday CRM
fit: The team wants configurable boards and shared sales processes.
catch: Three-seat minimum, then seat buckets. Smart Call is mobile-only and uses AI credits.
good: monday CRM gives teams flexible boards, ownership and automation. Pro includes sequences. Its Smart Call feature supports native calls in the mobile app with recording and summaries.
limit: Smart Call has no browser calling or power dialer. Reps calling from laptops need a separate phone integration.
cost: Pro costs $28 per seat per month on annual billing, or $41 monthly. Standard costs $17 or $25 on those terms. Four users pay for five seats; six pay for ten. Smart Call uses five AI credits per connected minute. Confirm the price of extra credits.
verdict: Good for shared pipelines and visual coordination. For a team power dialing from laptops, the extra phone setup makes it a less direct choice.
check: Price your next hire as well as today's headcount. Have a rep complete a real call and update the deal from the device they use all day.

name: Salesforce
fit: Your business needs custom sales processes and app integrations.
billing: Pro Suite, annual contract; Starter is $25
catch: Sales cadences and API access can add charges. Configuration needs an owner.
good: Starter offers basic CRM at a published price. Pro Suite adds more customization, quoting, forecasting and app integrations for a business with a defined sales process.
limit: Pro is four times Starter's seat price. It is easy to build a substantial bill around additional sales tools and administration. Confirm the exact edition needed for every integration.
cost: Starter is $25 per user monthly. Pro Suite is $100 with an annual contract. Its pricing table lists API access at another $25 per user monthly. Sales Engagement starts at $50 extra per user monthly, billed annually; confirm edition eligibility in the quote.
verdict: Starter is fairly priced for basic CRM work. Buy Pro when its customization and integrations solve a specific business need. The Salesforce name alone is a poor reason to pay more.
check: Ask for one quote covering the CRM, sales cadences, phone system, API needs and implementation. Get your own workflow demonstrated on that configuration.

name: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales
fit: Microsoft already runs the business and you have someone to manage setup.
catch: Teams calling has separate licence and phone requirements. Setup adds work.
good: Dynamics connects sales records with the Microsoft environment. Enterprise includes Sales Accelerator for up to 1,500 sequence-connected records a month, supporting organized follow-up.
limit: Professional has more limited automation. Teams calling needs separately licensed and configured phone service.
cost: Sales Professional is $65 per user monthly, Enterprise $105 and Premium $150, paid yearly. Phone service and some Power Platform capabilities need additional licences. The ten-seat minimum on Relationship Sales belongs to that separate LinkedIn bundle.
verdict: Dynamics suits a Microsoft-based business with someone responsible for the CRM. Budget for setup and administration. For a simple calling team, start with the easier options.
check: Test email sync and Teams calling with your actual licences. Confirm who will maintain permissions, fields and follow-up rules after launch.

name: Attio
fit: You want a configurable CRM for relationships and email follow-up.
catch: Sequences require Pro. Call Intelligence does not include an outbound phone service.
good: Attio offers flexible records, synced mailboxes and automation. Pro adds email sequences and more access controls. Its HubSpot migration route can bring across more than a basic CSV import.
limit: Attio describes sequences for warm leads, existing customers and expected messages. Phone calls need a separate integration. Check the workspace credit allowance for the automation and enrichment you plan to use.
cost: Free supports up to three seats. Plus costs $35 per user per month on annual billing, or $44 monthly. Pro costs $79 or $99 on those terms. All workspace members use the same plan. Calling providers and extra credits add charges.
verdict: Choose Attio for flexible customer records and relationship management. Daily cold calling needs a separate phone service, and Pro costs $79 per user on annual billing.
check: Move a small sample with linked companies, notes and deals. Test the phone integration and check which activities appear on the right record.
